_This page is generated from src/harnesses/index.ts, so it says what the tool does._

A harness is a coding agent's command-line program. `run` and `score` use the first installed harness in this order when you do not name one with `--harness`.

| Order | Id            | Executable     | Variable that names another executable |
| ----- | ------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| 1     | `pi`          | `pi`           | `SKILL_EVALS_BIN_PI`                   |
| 2     | `claude-code` | `claude`       | `SKILL_EVALS_BIN_CLAUDE_CODE`          |
| 3     | `cursor`      | `cursor-agent` | `SKILL_EVALS_BIN_CURSOR`               |
| 4     | `opencode`    | `opencode`     | `SKILL_EVALS_BIN_OPENCODE`             |
| 5     | `codex`       | `codex`        | `SKILL_EVALS_BIN_CODEX`                |

[How each harness is started](how-they-run.md) says why the order is what it is and when to set the variable. [What was verified](verified.md) says how far each adapter is proven.

## Isolation

`--isolated` starts the harness with nothing loaded but the subject, and invalidates a run whose own report of what it loaded shows anything else. The `isolated` capability means that the adapter does the first and proves the second from its report, so `--isolated` needs `loadedReport` too. A harness without both is a usage error that names it, raised before a run starts. Today `pi`, `cursor`, `opencode`, `codex` cannot run with it. Pi is started with discovery switched off (`-ne -ns -np`) whatever the flag says, and that stays its default, but it reports nothing it loaded, so it cannot run `--isolated` until an adapter can prove what it loaded. Flags are never trusted, and a harness that should report its plugins and skills but does not makes the run invalid with `the harness did not report what it loaded`. Under `--isolated` the judge, which loads nothing, gets the same switches when its harness can take them, and what it reports is held to the same rule.

| Harness       | Switches added by --isolated                                                     | What the report proves                                                                                                                                                      | Not proven                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `claude-code` | `--setting-sources user --strict-mcp-config` `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1` | Every plugin directory, plugin-prefixed skill and agent, and MCP server in the init event is the subject's. The report must list plugins and skills, or the run is invalid. | Managed policy settings (hooks, environment, permissions), managed memory and CLAUDE.md files, rules and hooks, and bare-named skills and agents, which are Claude Code's built-ins or the organization's managed ones: no switch removes them and the init event does not tell them apart. |

### What Claude Code does with these switches

- `--setting-sources user`: the CLI loads `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills`, the user's settings and the user's plugins only for the `user` source, and the workspace's `.claude/` skills and settings only for `project` and `local`. User level is the throwaway home, which holds only what the run puts there, such as the skills of a skills subject. An empty list (`""`) is accepted by the parser, but it would leave a skills subject unloaded.
- `--strict-mcp-config`: only the servers of `--mcp-config`. When an organization's enterprise MCP config is present the CLI refuses the flag and exits, which makes the run fail. A plugin's own MCP server is named `plugin:<plugin>:<server>` in the init event; every other server is outside the subject. Whether the flag also drops a plugin's own servers was not confirmed.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1` switches off auto memory.
- Never `--bare`: it also switches off the subject plugin's own hooks.
- A bare skill or agent name counts as a built-in, which is not outside the subject: any bare name that is not one of the subject's own skills. This includes skills from the organization's managed policy directory, which the CLI loads under every flag (the 2.1.330 code has no switch for it, and no `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_POLICY_SKILLS`). The init event does not tell the two apart, and the built-in names were not confirmed against a real capture. A plugin directory, a `plugin:`-prefixed skill or agent of another plugin, and an MCP server that is not the subject's are outside the subject.
- Organization-managed plugins load under every flag. The init event lists them, so the run is invalid.
- Not proven by the record: managed policy settings (hooks, environment, permissions), managed memory and `CLAUDE.md` files, rules and hooks. The report does not list them.
